confidence.reason: The complete static chain is visible in the single provided packet: line 6 takes $_REQUEST['ip'], line 9 splits it on '.', line 11 requires exactly four elements and is_numeric() on every one of the four parts, and line 13 rebuilds the string only from those four parts joined by '.'. A PHP numeric string can contain only leading whitespace (and trailing whitespace since PHP 8.0), an optional sign, digits, an optional fraction and exponent, plus the pre-PHP 7.0 0x hexadecimal form; none of those characters is a shell control operator (';', '|', '&', '$', backtick, '(', ')', '<', '>', quotes) or can produce one. The sink at lines 17 and 21 therefore always receives a dotted numeric token, so the executed command remains 'ping [-c 4] <token>', and the non-numeric fallback at line 28 returns an error without calling the interpreter.

The deployed PHP version is unknown; is_numeric() semantics differ by version (0x hexadecimal strings accepted before PHP 7.0, trailing whitespace accepted from PHP 8.0), which shifts the exact set of characters that can survive the whitelist.

Operating system, shell (/bin/sh versus cmd.exe), ping availability and whether shell_exec is disabled through disable_functions are unverified; both OS branches exist in the code but were not executed.

risk_notes: Argument/option injection (outside the declared command-injection scope): signed numeric octets such as '-1' pass is_numeric(), so $target can begin with '-' and be parsed by ping as an option rather than a host; this was not verified and is not shell command execution.

Output handling: $cmd is interpolated into "
{$cmd}
" without HTML escaping, so any attacker-influenced text in ping output would become an HTML-injection surface; whether ping output can be influenced by a dotted numeric token is unconfirmed.
Input surface: 'ip' is read through $_REQUEST (not $_POST), so the same value may be supplied via GET or Cookie while the trigger remains $_POST['Submit'].
CSRF protection is present; a missing or expired token redirects instead of reaching the ping call, which is an authentication-state precondition, not a vulnerability.
quality_notes: shell_exec() is called with string concatenation instead of escapeshellarg()/escapeshellcmd() or a proc_open() argument array; the structural fix is to validate with filter_var($target, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP) and then still escape the argument.
$_REQUEST is used for 'ip' while the trigger uses $_POST['Submit'], widening the input surface unnecessarily.
The comment 'Check IF each octet is an integer' is inaccurate: is_numeric() also accepts signs, exponents, fractions and (by PHP version) hexadecimal or whitespace-padded forms.
stripslashes() is a legacy magic_quotes-era idiom that has no effect on shell metacharacters here.
limitations: This is a static review of one 33-line normalized fragment; no request, ping, shell command or target system was executed, so runtime_evidence is empty.
The exclusion covers only this code path; an outer handler that was not supplied could filter or rewrite 'ip' before the fragment is included, and other pages were out of scope.

Numeric strings may still contain leading whitespace (and trailing whitespace on PHP 8.0+) including newline, which a shell can use as a command separator; however the text after any such newline is again a dotted numeric token, so no attacker-chosen command is reachable. This boundary depends on the deployed PHP version and shell and should be regression-tested.

The conclusion is a static judgment; confirmation of safety would require running the fragment on the actual PHP/OS configuration with payloads containing shell metacharacters and whitespace variants.
